segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The carving fills the whole north wall: a rugged mountain riddled with tunnels, rays of sunrise fanning out from its peak. In its caverns stand thirty-two tiny dwarves, cut mid-song, mouths open, beards braided into the seams of the rock. It is old dwarven work, patient and loving. Below it the long stone tub sits sunk into the floor.

segments.speaker: Dealer
segments.text: You admire the old stonework, little scholar? The dwarves who cut it are long gone, and they left their singing behind for us to ignore. It is a poor sort of company. The cards, at least, answer back. Will you not come and sit where the light is better?

segments.speaker: Kit
segments.text: Do you go back to the table?
segments.reacts_to: Will you not come and sit
